title: Two-Time World Champion Nikhat Zareen Knocked Out of CWG and Asian Games Trials

body:
Nikhat Zareen, India's two-time World Championship gold medallist, suffered a stunning 1-4 loss to Sakshi Chaudhary in the women's 51kg semifinal at the National Boxing Trials in Patiala on Wednesday, ending her hopes of competing at both the 2026 Commonwealth Games and Asian Games.

The defeat marks the sharpest setback in Zareen's decorated career. The Telangana-born boxer, who became a household name after her Paris Olympics campaign and consecutive world titles, appeared drained and off-rhythm against Chaudhary, a 2023 World Championships gold medallist who recently moved down from the 54kg category.

Zareen did not mince words after the bout. She described the entire selection process as 'torturous for boxers,' pointing to months of administrative chaos between the Boxing Federation of India (BFI) and the Sports Authority of India (SAI) over whether to use assessment-based selection or traditional trials. The dispute left athletes in limbo for weeks, forced to maintain strict weight cuts without knowing when — or whether — they would compete.

The BFI ultimately reverted to the trial system after SAI suspended the assessment-based approach, a move broadly welcomed by boxers as more transparent. But Zareen, who had been unable to compete at the Asian Championships earlier this year, came into Patiala ring-rusty and mentally spent.

For the diaspora sports community that has followed Zareen's rise as one of Indian women's boxing's most visible champions, her exit signals a generational shift. Sakshi Chaudhary and Meenakshi Hooda, both in their early twenties, now lead India's 51kg challenge. Zareen, 30, says she will focus on rebuilding fitness for the LA 2028 Olympic qualifiers — but the road just got steeper.
